body:
Confirmed on `v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]`, even with reasonably low sort values for the overlapping decals (e.g. `2`).

There is a note on the Decal documentation about flickering decals as the camera moves for the Mobile renderer, but the MRP is using Forward+ with only 2 decals on the affected mesh, and it isn't a flicker here. Swapping to Mobile does result in only 8 decals being shown on the second mesh, but the ordering problem does not occur like it does in Forward+. This is true even if I duplicate the second mesh enough times to have 32 rendered decals with the Mobile renderer.

> Note: Decals are only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, not Compatibility. When using the Mobile rendering method, only 8 decals can be displayed on each mesh resource. Attempting to display more than 8 decals on a single mesh resource will result in decals flickering in and out as the camera moves.

```
Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 (Apple7) - Apple M1 (8 threads)
```

@takdew Interestingly, I was researching the exact same thing today and came to the same conclusion. Godot seems to split decals into groups of 32 and sort them within their respective subgroup. So even if you have your max_clustered_elements set high in your project settings, it doesn't affect the sorting because the decals on screen are all divided into these sets of 32.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7826b6b13fccf57d1461794afc560853c4d2531d/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_clustered.glsl#L1476-L1489

This appears to be a limitation of using a bitmask to handle the depth sorting of decals. I'm wondering if it is possible for cluster buffers to instead use a sorted array of decal indeces as opposed to a bitmask.

I also found this, but I'm a bit confused as to how this plays into everything. I assumed this decal_sort array was used for passing data into the cluster buffer in the correct order, but my assumption is that it would sort all decals in the scene, not just per subgroup.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7c472e655f974e1f41ff086fa448c94c220728a2/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp#L3133-L3136

The important distinction is that, from my observations, the decals are placed in subgroups based on when they are added to the decal buffer. Meaning, the first 32 decals added to the buffer are sorted together, and then any subsequently added decals become part of the next subgroup, and so on. This is strange to me because if the aforementioned decal_sort sorts all visible decals based on their depth, my understanding is that it should be sending that data to the cluster buffer in the same order, which would then place them in the relevant subgroup. Instead, the subgroups are based on the order of when the decals were added. I could be misinterpreting this, however.

Are there any resources that I can read to better understand this algorithm? I think it has something to do with clustering, but I don't quite get the purpose behind e.g.
```hlsl
		item_from = subgroupBroadcastFirst(subgroupMin(item_from));
		item_to = subgroupBroadcastFirst(subgroupMax(item_to));
```
I'm willing to fix this, but sadly I lack any experience with writing rendering code.

Fixing this issue is important to me, because the environment I'm currently making has a lot of detail, with decals count pushing few thousands.

> Are there any resources that I can read to better understand this algorithm?

I suggest joining the [Godot Contributors Chat](https://chat.godotengine.org/) and asking in the `#rendering` channel.
Are there any workarounds for this? Or is it planned to be fixed somewhen?

For those wondering about a workaround, here's what I can think of (neither solves the problem, but maybe can help you achieve your goals another way):

- Make some decals be part of object's material. That does not seem to be always applicable, but in some cases -- maybe
- Disable decal batching at all 🙂 (not sure this is easy to do in engine code... and maybe the performance will become unacceptable)
- Make some decals simple plains with alpha-scissor material and put them very close to the surface to guarantee they are drawn on top (not always applicable, but sometimes this can be a "good-enough" solution)
